Deeper wells. Hotter ground. Harder on fluids.
MinterEllison flagged it last week: Todd Energy is the preferred lead drilling contractor for the Rotokawa superhot geothermal programme near Taupō. Wells 1 to 3 km deeper than traditional geothermal. Up to $60 million from the Regional Infrastructure Fund backing it.

That's a big deal for NZ drilling.

Deeper holes mean higher temperatures, longer trips, and more time for the fluid to do its job downhole. Carrier performance, filtration control, and clay inhibition all get tested harder the deeper you go.

Programmes like this lift the standard for everyone working in geothermal and deep exploration. Worth watching.
Anyone in the NZ geothermal space, what are you seeing on the ground? Always keen to hear what's working.

Your bore's tightening up. Rods are dragging. Returns are getting gluggy.
Sounds like reactive clay.

Here's what's happening downhole. Some clays and shales soak up water like a sponge. When your water-based mud hits them, they swell. The hole closes in around your tooling. Cuttings break down into sticky fines that thicken your returns. Worst case, you stick the string.

Winter makes it worse. Wetter ground, higher water content in the formation, more reactive clay activity. The mud you got away with in summer suddenly isn't enough.

The fix is inhibition. You stop the clay from absorbing water in the first place. That's what **Clay Control** is built for. Locks the clay down so it stays where it belongs and your hole stays open.

Friday I'll go deeper on how to use it, when to pair it with other products, and the ground conditions where it earns its keep.
What ground are you fighting this winter? Drop a comment.
#ClayControl #DrillingFluids #BlickFluids #ReactiveClay #BoreStability #HDD #WaterWell #DrillingAustralia #DrillingNZ

Clay Control. Here's when it earns its place in your fluid program.
Wednesday we covered the problem: reactive clays swell, hole tightens, rods bind.

Clay Control is the inhibitor that stops it. Use it when you're drilling through shale, mudstone, or any ground where clay content is high and the formation is wet. HDD crews working river crossings and wet coastal ground get the most out of it. Water well drillers hitting reactive layers between aquifers, same story.

Pair it smart. **Swell Stop Dry** or **Swell Stop Liquid** alongside Clay Control when the ground is properly nasty. **Filter Low** to keep the wall cake tight so less fluid invades the formation in the first place. Less invasion, less swelling, cleaner hole.

For dosage rates, follow the product data sheet. For tougher conditions, give one of our team a call. We'll dial in the right program for the ground you're in, not a generic recipe off a bag.

That's how you keep a bore open through winter.
Got a job coming up where the ground worries you? Call us before you mix. Quicker than fixing it mid-bore.
